name: Gjipe
blurb: A small white-pebble beach set below cliffs at the mouth of a wooded gorge, with clear water, a seasonal cafe and not much else. Recently voted one of the best beaches in the world, and still quiet by Mediterranean standards.

name: Ksamil
blurb: Still, glistening bays and small islets you can swim to, at the southern tip of the Riviera near Butrint. Abundant, busy and warm in season.

name: Sarande
blurb: The southern gateway: a horseshoe bay, a long esplanade, ferries to Corfu forty minutes across the channel. The Discovery tour settles here for three nights.

name: Himara old town
blurb: Narrow cobbled laneways, a ruined fortress and olive trees above the Ionian. The old hill settlement is slowly being restored while the beach town gets on with summer below.

name: Dhermi and the Riviera beaches
blurb: A hundred and twenty kilometres of coastline running from busy Sarande to coves you will have to yourself: Dhermi, Jal, Gjipe and the rest, threaded by one very scenic road over the Llogara pass.

name: Porto Palermo
blurb: A quiet bay with an early 19th-century fort built by Ali Pasha, good for a swim and a wander. The legend says he built it for his much younger wife inside 24 hours.

name: Theth
blurb: A stone village deep in the Accursed Mountains: the shingled church, the Grunasa waterfall, the Tower of Isolation and some of the best walking in the Balkans.

name: Valbona
blurb: A high glacial valley at a thousand metres, walled by two-thousand-metre peaks, with a braided white river bed running its length. The pass walk from Theth is the classic.

name: Lake Komani
blurb: A 34-kilometre reservoir threading magnificent fjord-like gorges, crossed by ferry between walls of rock and forest on mirror-still green water.

name: The Vjosa and Permet
blurb: One of Europe's last wild rivers, running turquoise and undammed for 270 kilometres. At Permet the draw is thermal springs, the Lengarica canyon and slow food done properly.

name: The Blue Eye
blurb: A natural spring rising from a karst hole at a constant ten degrees, so clear and so blue it looks lit from below. The source of the Bistrica river, in the hills behind Sarande.

name: Bovilla
blurb: A turquoise reservoir folded into the ridges near Tirana, with rock climbing and a clifftop lookout above the water.

name: Berat
blurb: The town of a thousand windows: a 2,400-year-old UNESCO city of white Ottoman houses stacked above the Osum, with an inhabited castle you can sleep inside.

name: Gjirokastra
blurb: The City of Stone: 2,500 years old, UNESCO-listed, with one of the largest castles in the Balkans and a cobbled bazaar where the shops still spill onto the street.

name: Butrint
blurb: Two hundred hectares of Greek and Roman ruins in coastal woodland: a theatre, a forum and Byzantine mosaics, and the country's largest archaeological site.

name: Kruja
blurb: Skanderbeg's mountain stronghold: the castle and museum, the ethnographic house, and an old bazaar that has been trading on the same cobbles for centuries.

name: Apollonia
blurb: An ancient Illyrian city founded in 588 BC, its theatre and colonnades standing in open farmland with a monastery museum alongside.

name: Tirana
blurb: A capital that mixes ages and cultures at speed: Skanderbeg Square, Bunk'Art 2 and the House of Leaves, the Bllok's cafes, the new bazaar and a cable car up Dajti.

name: Shkodra
blurb: A lively university town under Rozafa castle, where the lake, the Alps and some of Albania's best museums sit within one easy stay.

name: Korca
blurb: Cobblestone streets, parks and beer gardens around the domed cathedral, an old bazaar, and Albania's oldest brewery. The gateway to Voskopoja's painted churches.

name: Lake Ohrid
blurb: One of Europe's deepest and oldest lakes, shared with North Macedonia and so clear it filters like spring water. The Balkans Explorer crosses to the Bay of Bones stilt village on its far shore.
